seed: The panel beside a recording, at the smallest window the app supports, with nothing switched from its default. It leads with what the picked layer is FOR: a clip's Time, Sound and Animating, a title's Time, Text and Animating, a sound's Sound. Every row is a short label and a value, inset like the rest of the panel, and the speed, the level and the fade are on screen without scrolling.

steps.note: THE FIRST TEST: an eight second recording picked in a 1200 by 720 window. Under Layers the panel says how it plays (Time: Speed, Length, Sound), how loud (Sound: Level), then what is keyed (Animating). No paragraph anywhere, no Reframe section, and every row starts on the same margin as the rest of the panel

THE SECOND TEST: speed is ONE dropdown, the one a Premiere editor reaches for in Speed/Duration. Picking 2x halves the bar on the timeline, the Length row reads 8s into 4s and the Sound row says it plays higher. The silent speeds say (silent) on their own row in the menu
THE THIRD TEST: Punch In is a right-click preset on the clip, around the spot you clicked, not a section of its own. What it did is the clip's ordinary Scale and Position, keyed, read in Animating
THE FOURTH TEST: a title picked. Under Layers: when it is on screen and how it fades (Time), its words (Text), then what is keyed. The Fade dropdown is on screen without scrolling
THE FIFTH TEST: a piece of music picked. The panel leads with its Level, straight under Layers, on screen without scrolling
